actor: Infrastructure financial planning and analysis lead, hyperscale advertising platform
job: Building a standalone profit-and-loss view for external compute and AI services so the chief operating decision maker reviews it discretely.
outcome: A monthly management package carrying compute revenue, cost and margin as their own reviewed lines rather than an advertising overhead.
motivation: A reported segment requires discrete financial information the decision maker already reviews; without the internal cut there is nothing to publish.

task.who: Infrastructure finance and corporate planning teams
task.what: Carve a standalone compute P&L into the management package
task.where: Monthly management reporting package and internal planning systems
task.why: No internal cut means no reportable line to publish
task.how: Cost allocation model splitting internal from external compute

actor: Datacenter capacity planning lead, large-scale AI infrastructure operator
job: Ring-fencing the accelerator capacity that can be sold externally from the fleet reserved for the company's own ranking and training workloads.
outcome: A measurable pool of externally sellable capacity with its own utilisation and cost basis, separable from internal consumption.
motivation: Capital expenditure of $130-145 billion is divisible into a revenue line only if some of that capacity is measured as external.

task.who: Capacity planning and infrastructure engineering teams
task.what: Ring-fence externally sellable accelerator capacity from the internal fleet
task.where: Fleet capacity planning systems and datacenter allocation reviews
task.why: External revenue needs capacity measured apart from internal use
task.how: Capacity tagging with internal transfer pricing per accelerator hour

actor: Enterprise compute commercial lead, cloud infrastructure business unit
job: Converting the premium offers already being made for the company's compute into signed multi-year external supply contracts.
outcome: Signed external compute contracts with billable committed capacity, large enough that the resulting revenue cannot stay immaterial by design.
motivation: Management says it is offered a significant premium over what the compute cost, and the enterprise opportunity is already named.

task.who: Enterprise sales, deal desk and contracting teams
task.what: Sign multi-year external compute supply contracts
task.where: Enterprise deal desk and customer contract negotiations
task.why: There is no line to report without external revenue
task.how: Committed-capacity agreements with take-or-pay minimums and premium pricing

actor: Product lead for enterprise AI services monetisation
job: Making business agents and inference services separately metered and billable so their revenue can be counted apart from advertising.
outcome: A billing system producing an auditable external revenue figure for agent and inference usage every reporting period.
motivation: The stated preference is to sell intelligence rather than compute, and an intelligence business needs a disclosed line just as much.

task.who: Monetisation product management and billing platform engineering
task.what: Ship metered billing for enterprise agent and inference usage
task.where: The enterprise billing platform and usage metering pipeline
task.why: Unmetered usage cannot become an auditable reported revenue line
task.how: Usage metering instrumentation feeding rated invoices and a revenue subledger

actor: Investor relations director, mega-cap technology issuer
job: Preparing the disclosure that gives the capital expenditure a denominator, so the next spending raise is read the way Azure's was.
outcome: A results release and call script that names external compute and AI-services revenue with its own dollar figure.
motivation: The same spending case moved one stock up fifteen percent and the other down; the difference was a disclosed revenue line.

task.who: Investor relations and financial communications teams
task.what: Quantify external compute demand at the fourth-quarter results release
task.where: The quarterly results release, earnings call and analyst follow-ups
task.why: A larger spending guide needs a denominator investors can see
task.how: Prepared remarks, disclosure committee review and sell-side pre-briefings

actor: Technical revenue accounting manager, corporate controllership
job: Settling how external compute contracts are recognised, gross or net and service or lease, before any figure can be reported.
outcome: A documented recognition policy for capacity contracts that survives audit and supports a separately captioned revenue figure.
motivation: A new revenue caption cannot be published until its recognition, presentation and disaggregation conclusions are documented and defensible.

task.who: Technical accounting and controllership policy teams
task.what: Document recognition policy for external compute capacity contracts
task.where: Accounting policy memoranda and the auditor review process
task.why: An undocumented policy blocks any separately captioned revenue figure
task.how: Revenue standard analysis covering gross-versus-net and lease scoping

actor: Disclosure review staff, securities market regulator
job: Reviewing the annual filing's segment and revenue disaggregation and questioning whether a growing external compute business stays inside other revenue.
outcome: A comment letter forcing the issuer to justify or abandon burying compute revenue in an undifferentiated other line.
motivation: Disaggregation rules require categories depicting how economics differ, and a $130-145 billion spending programme with no revenue line invites that question.

task.who: Corporation finance disclosure review and accounting staff
task.what: Issue comment letters on segment and revenue disaggregation
task.where: The filing review process and public comment-letter correspondence
task.why: Regulator pressure turns an optional breakout into a required one
task.how: Filing review against segment reporting and disaggregation standards

actor: Segment reporting controller, external financial reporting
job: Re-cutting the four-line revenue table so external compute and AI services carry their own caption with restated comparatives.
outcome: A quarterly revenue table showing external compute and AI-services revenue as a named line beside advertising and other revenue.
motivation: Reality Labs became a reported segment only when its spending needed a table of its own; the same test now applies to compute.

task.who: External reporting and segment accounting teams
task.what: Draft the compute revenue caption and restate prior comparatives
task.where: Quarterly results release tables and the periodic filing
task.why: The caption and its comparatives must exist before publication
task.how: Segment reporting standard applied through the consolidation system
